summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of CVA, tracheostomy, ileostomy, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and prior Pseudomonas pneumonia was admitted from a skilled nursing facility for fever and hypotension. He was found to have sepsis likely from pneumonia and a urinary tract infection caused by Proteus stuartii. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin, meropenem, and ciprofloxacin. His condition improved with stabilization of vital signs, resolution of fever, and decreasing white blood cell count. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotic administration. His atrial fibrillation required temporary discontinuation of Coumadin due to supratherapeutic INR, and he was rate-controlled with metoprolol. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. Thrush was treated with nystatin, and his stage III sacral ulcer was managed with wound care and pain control. He was discharged to extended care on a 10-day course of IV and oral antibiotics with close INR and blood sugar monitoring.
